question: Does showing the problem immediately in a closer opening outperform the wider setup?

phases.name: calibration
phases.purpose: Workflow, comprehension and how much results vary from post to post. Not part of the comparison.

phases.name: experimental
phases.purpose: The comparison, randomised within premise families.

phases.name: confirmation
phases.purpose: New premises: does the direction hold? Directional evidence only.

variants.A: Closer opening: the character and the problem are both in shot and readable from frame 0
variants.B: The wider setup, no title card

audience: Viewers of absurd character comedy who don't know the cast
cast: Phoenix and Reaper (docs/character-bible.md); the Wizard occasionally
fixed: music seeded per episode (both arms draw from the same styles)
assignment: Write all premises first, group them into families by situation and complexity, then randomise A or B within each family. Don't give the strongest ideas to one arm.
primaryOutcome: views at 7 days, TikTok and Shorts compared separately
threshold: PROPOSED, to confirm before the first experimental post: A is worth keeping if its mean log(1+views) at 7 days is at least 0.22 higher than B's (about 25 % more views for a typical post) on both platforms, it leads in at least 4 of the 6 premise families, and the closer opening costs no more than 10 extra minutes per episode.
decisionRule: Keep the closer opening as the default only if it clears the threshold and the confirmation batch points the same way. Otherwise keep B and treat the result as unresolved, not as proof that openings don't matter.
costGuardrail: Active minutes per episode, logged in results.csv
notes: Before the experimental phase: show drafts privately to 5-8 people who don't know the cast and ask what happened and what surprised them, without explaining the joke.
